answer: Each identity proves live custody of a basalt block, a 40-kilogram chunk of rock fitted with a sealed load cell, imaged on a fixed knoll site at a random epoch time. Registrars publish the cell stream and the image hash; any custodian reruns the check, and two identities reporting one block's stream in the same epoch expose shared custody and forfeit both deposits. One honest agent hauls and guards one block. A farm of 1,000 identities must haul and station 1,000 distinct blocks, each watched by a vine camera trained on its own block, and cannot lend one block to two names.
